patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a small rectangular input-like box in the top navigation area, positioned at the upper right on desktop and near the top section on mobile, which strongly implies a site/page search control.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should support text entry and search submission; may also include focus handling, placeholder behavior, and possibly live suggestions if implemented beyond a basic submit search.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not reveal whether results are live/autocomplete or only submitted on Enter/button press.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch has a distinct top horizontal utility/navigation row separated from the long article body below, suggesting a persistent header treatment for a content-heavy page.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented as sticky, the top nav/search area should remain accessible while scrolling through the long document-like content.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show a fixed state during scroll; this is inferred from the long-form layout and isolated header band.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a mostly static, article-style page with minimal JavaScript needs. The clearest interactive requirement across both viewports is a search field in the header area. Desktop additionally suggests a persistent top navigation/header treatment because the page is long and document-like, while mobile appears simplified and stacked without any clearly drawn hamburger, dropdown, accordion, modal, or load-more behavior.
